topics.title: Polling (Chat System)
topics.description: Understanding polling techniques used in chat systems, including short polling and long polling, their scalability implications, and comparison with WebSocket.

subtopics.title: Definition
subtopics.theory:
1️⃣ Definition

Polling is a communication technique in which a client repeatedly sends requests to a server at fixed or conditional intervals to check whether new data is available.

Instead of the server pushing updates automatically, the client actively asks for updates.

In chat systems, polling is used to check for new messages.

subtopics.title: Why Polling Exists
subtopics.theory:
2️⃣ Why Polling Exists

The HTTP protocol is:

Request–response based

Client-initiated

Stateless

The server cannot send data unless the client asks for it.

So polling was historically used to simulate “real-time” behavior over HTTP.

subtopics.title: Types of Polling
subtopics.theory:
3️⃣ Types of Polling

There are two major types:

subtopics.title: Short Polling
subtopics.theory:
A) Short Polling

🔹 Definition

Short polling is a method where the client sends requests to the server at fixed time intervals (e.g., every 2 seconds), regardless of whether new data exists.



🔹 Flow of Short Polling

Client sends HTTP request:

GET /messages?since=123

Server checks database.

Server returns:

New messages (if available)

Or empty response

Client waits for predefined interval (e.g., 2 sec)

Client repeats request

This loop continues indefinitely.



🔹 Important Characteristics

Connection is opened and closed for every request

Uses HTTP protocol

Each request includes full HTTP headers

TCP connection must be established repeatedly



🔹 Example Calculation (Scalability Problem)

Suppose:

5 million users

Each polls every 5 seconds

Requests per second:

5,000,000 / 5 = 1,000,000 requests per second

Even if no one sends messages.

This is inefficient.

subtopics.title: Long Polling
subtopics.theory:
B) Long Polling

Long polling attempts to improve short polling.



🔹 Definition

Long polling is a technique where the client sends a request and the server keeps the connection open until:

New data becomes available, OR

A timeout occurs



🔹 Flow of Long Polling

Client sends request:

GET /messages?since=123

Server checks for new messages.

If no message:

Server does NOT respond immediately

Holds request open

If message arrives:

Server responds immediately

Client receives response

Client immediately sends another request



🔹 Timeout Handling

If no message arrives within a threshold (e.g., 30 seconds):

Server returns empty response

Client reconnects

This ensures the connection does not remain open forever.

subtopics.title: Important System Design Points
subtopics.theory:
4️⃣ Important System Design Points



1. Latency

Latency = delay between message sent and message received.

Short polling latency depends on interval.

If polling interval = 5 sec

Worst-case delay = 5 sec

Long polling latency ≈ near real-time



2. Server Resource Usage

Every polling request consumes:

A thread or async worker

Memory

Network buffer

CPU cycles

With millions of users → high cost.



3. TCP Handshake Overhead

Every new HTTP request requires:

TCP 3-way handshake

Request header transmission

Response header transmission

Connection close

This overhead repeats continuously.



4. Bandwidth Waste

In short polling:

Most responses are empty

Still consume bandwidth

This increases infrastructure cost.

subtopics.title: Advantages of Polling
subtopics.theory:
5️⃣ Advantages of Polling



✅ Simple Implementation

Works using standard HTTP

No special protocol required

Easy to implement in backend frameworks



✅ Firewall Friendly

Works over HTTP/HTTPS

No special network configuration needed



✅ Backward Compatible

Works on legacy browsers

Works in restricted corporate environments



✅ Stateless Model

Each request independent → easier horizontal scaling.

subtopics.title: Disadvantages of Polling
subtopics.theory:
6️⃣ Disadvantages of Polling



❌ Poor Scalability

Repeated requests increase linearly with users.

Scaling becomes expensive.



❌ High Infrastructure Cost

More:

Servers

Load balancers

Network bandwidth



❌ Higher Latency (Short Polling)

Delay depends on polling frequency.



❌ Connection Overhead

Repeated:

TCP handshakes

HTTP header transmission

Inefficient for real-time systems.



❌ Thread Blocking (Long Polling)

If using thread-per-request model:

Millions of long polling connections

Huge memory usage

Risk of thread exhaustion

subtopics.title: Why Polling is Not Ideal for Large Chat Systems
subtopics.theory:
7️⃣ Why Polling is Not Ideal for Large Chat Systems

Modern chat systems like:

WhatsApp

Messenger

Slack

Discord

Have:

Millions of concurrent connections

Real-time delivery requirement

Low latency expectations

Polling creates:

Too many redundant requests

Too much overhead

Poor performance at scale

Therefore, they use WebSocket.

subtopics.title: Technical Terms
subtopics.theory:
8️⃣ Technical Terms (Deep Definitions)



🔹 HTTP (Hypertext Transfer Protocol)

Application-layer protocol used for communication between web clients and servers. It follows request-response model.



🔹 TCP (Transmission Control Protocol)

Transport-layer protocol that ensures reliable data delivery using handshake and acknowledgments.



🔹 3-Way Handshake

Process of establishing TCP connection:

SYN

SYN-ACK

ACK



🔹 Latency

Total delay from message send to message delivery.

Includes:

Network delay

Server processing

Queue delay



🔹 Timeout

Maximum duration server keeps connection open before responding.



🔹 Stateless Architecture

Server does not retain session information between requests.



🔹 Horizontal Scaling

Adding more servers to distribute load.



🔹 Concurrent Users

Users connected at same time.



🔹 Blocking vs Non-Blocking I/O

Blocking: Thread waits until operation completes.
Non-blocking: Thread can handle multiple operations.

Important for long polling scalability.

subtopics.title: When to Use Polling
subtopics.theory:
🔟 When to Use Polling

Use polling when:

Small user base (<10k concurrent users)

Real-time not critical

Infrastructure simple

Prototyping stage

Limited backend capabilities

Avoid polling when:

Real-time required

Millions of users

Mobile battery optimization important

High-performance systems

subtopics.title: Final Interview Summary
subtopics.theory:
🏁 Final Interview-Ready Summary

Polling is a client-driven data retrieval mechanism over HTTP. While simple and widely compatible, it generates high overhead and scales poorly in real-time, large-scale systems. For massive chat applications, persistent bi-directional protocols like WebSocket are superior due to reduced latency and connection overhead.
